events.subtitle: The Music of The Crusaders
events.factual_description: Keystone Korner Baltimore and its authorized InstantSeats page present Phaze II: The Music of The Crusaders on Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 7:00 PM. The exact event page lists Karen Linette on vocals, Adrian "Egg" Norton on bass, Steve Perkins on percussion, Brent Birckhead on saxophone, Trendle Thomas on keyboards, David Suggs Sr. on drums, Kenny Saunders on guitar and Curtis Jones on trombone. InstantSeats lists live tickets at $30-$35 plus fees, while Visit Baltimore independently lists the event from 7:00 to 8:30 PM and describes Phaze II as a Washington, DC-area smooth/funky jazz band active since 1997. The event framing centers The Crusaders' electric jazz/R&B/soul/fusion period and specifically references catalog touchstones including Street Life, Soul Shadows, Keep That Same Old Feeling and Way Back Home; this description records the presenter's framing and does not infer a performed setlist.

en.why_it_matters: This is more specific than a smooth-jazz club date: a long-running Washington-area groove band is taking an expanded eight-person lineup into The Crusaders' electric language, where jazz met R&B, soul and funk without giving up instrumental interplay. Bass, percussion, drums, guitar, keys, saxophone, trombone and vocals give Phaze II the palette to approach that catalog as living band music rather than museum tribute. It is a useful Baltimore night for anyone following the groove-and-fusion thread.
en.trip_verdict: If a Thursday run to Baltimore fits the week, this is worth the short trip and an easy event to pair with dinner at the club. I would not restructure a corridor weekend around it: the appeal is the repertoire-specific DMV groove connection, not a scarce appearance by surviving Crusaders personnel.
en.listen_before: The Crusaders — Street Life; Phaze II — Live N Uncut

es.why_it_matters: Esto es más concreto que una fecha cualquiera de smooth jazz: una banda del área de Washington con casi tres décadas de groove lleva una formación ampliada de ocho músicos al lenguaje eléctrico de The Crusaders, donde jazz, R&B, soul y funk se cruzaban sin perder el juego instrumental. Bajo, percusión, batería, guitarra, teclados, sax, trombón y voz le dan a Phaze II una paleta suficiente para tratar ese repertorio como música viva de banda y no como pieza de museo. Es una buena parada en Baltimore para seguir el hilo de groove y fusión.
es.trip_verdict: Si el jueves permite la escapada a Baltimore, vale el viaje corto y se presta para combinarlo con cena en el club. No reorganizaría un fin de semana del corredor alrededor de esta fecha: el atractivo está en el cruce entre repertorio de The Crusaders y una banda del DMV, no en una aparición escasa de integrantes históricos del grupo.
